title: Microsoft Clipchamp: Copilot video creation in Video Hub, billed in Copilot Credits
summary: Hold: the spending-policy route omits the required Identity scope choice, and the page overstates the need for fresh administrator enablement despite automatic coverage of new services. Its claims that the watermark policy and Anthropic data-boundary exclusion have unconfirmed applicability also disregard the documented reach of those rules.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationales: risk, impact; Open questions
claims.claim: Admin-opt-in means doing nothing prevents access until an administrator specifically enables this feature in a spending policy.
claims.quote: Spending policies can automatically apply to future supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents. ... No action is required when you want future supported services and agents to inherit the policy.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown and replace the unconditional no-action claims with: 'The notice requires Anthropic access and a spending policy covering the feature. Learn says Auto-apply new services can automatically cover newly supported services, and Anthropic is already on by default for most commercial tenants outside EU/EFTA and UK; do not assume fresh enablement is required.' Retain the notice's prerequisites, but replace the Auto-apply open question with the documented automatic-coverage rule. Apply this qualification to the risk and impact rationales too. Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/connect-to-ai-subprocessor.

claims.quote: Customers within the EU Data Boundary and customers in the UK have Claude models disabled by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions: EU Data Boundary
claims.claim: It is not stated whether the Claude EU Data Boundary exclusion covers video creation.
claims.quote: Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings such as Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary
claims.fix: Remove 'Whether that page's statement covers video creation is not stated' and the corresponding EU Data Boundary applicability question. Replace the caveat with: 'The exclusion is stated for Claude models deployed in Microsoft offerings; the notice requires Anthropic models for this feature.' The list introduced by 'such as' is not an exhaustive feature list. Keep the separately open question about regional availability at general availability.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The identity-based spending-policy path is Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Select agents and services.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter and the rendered table with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Define the policy scope > Identity > Select agents and services'. The Identity scope is a required workflow choice, not merely an omitted heading; names, group selection and Next can remain omitted under the verification standard. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row

claims.claim: The update operation documents displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and billingMethods as updatable, not selection of services.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The Graph operation is beta and subject to change.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.claim: The notice says exported videos carry a Made with AI watermark that admins can turn off.
claims.quote: Exported videos carry a "Made with AI" watermark, which admins can turn off.

claims.claim: Learn gives a video generated with Clipchamp as an example of a visual watermark.
claims.quote: A visual watermark is added to a video generated with Clipchamp.

claims.claim: Learn says its watermark policy must be Enabled for a visual or audio watermark to be added.
claims.quote: If you want to add a watermark to video and audio content, you need to set this policy to Enabled. If you set this policy to Disabled or Not configured, a visual or audio watermark isn't added.

claims.claim: The watermark policy is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: This policy is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Governance controls: Watermark; Open questions: watermark setting
claims.claim: Learn does not state that its Cloud Policy watermark control governs the video creation experience in the notice.
claims.quote: A policy setting controls your organization's ability to add a visual or audio watermark to video and audio content that your users generate or alter by using AI in Microsoft 365. ... A visual watermark is added to a video generated with Clipchamp.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence denying documented applicability with: 'Learn documents the Include a watermark when content from Microsoft 365 is generated or altered by AI policy for AI-generated video and audio in Microsoft 365, explicitly including Clipchamp video. The notice describes a Made with AI watermark, while Learn says its policy must be Enabled; confirm the differing default descriptions in your tenant.' Replace the open question about whether the policy applies with a question about the differing default descriptions. Do not add a control row as part of this correction. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/watermarks.

claims.claim: The notice and Learn give different descriptions of whether a video watermark is present without enabling a policy.
claims.quote: You need to enable a policy setting for watermarks to be added to video and audio content.
